text: Let's start by asking how long you've had this knee swelling and if there has been any trauma. Do you experience pain, redness, or warmth in the joint, and does the swelling fluctuate throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pigmented Villonodular Synovitis (PVNS) or Familial Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA). Given the age, swelling duration, and family history, I suspect a chronic inflammatory or proliferative synovial process. Please have the parents bring the patient for a MRI of the right knee to assess for synovial thickening or bone erosion. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Right_Knee
